```{r step6, message=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
           ": capital below T-Bill face value required for initial margin")
    }

    # ── T-bill P&L for week t ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    # DTB3 is annualised percent (e.g. 5.25 = 5.25% p.a.).
    # Weekly return: (1 + DTB3/100)^(7/365.25) - 1
    # Applied to free cash only (capital minus margin posted).
    rate_t        <- dtb3_t[t]
    weekly_ret_t  <- if (!is.na(rate_t) && rate_t > 0) {
      (1 + rate_t / 100)^(7 / 365.25) - 1
    } else {
      0
    }
    tbill_pnl_t   <- idle_cash_t * weekly_ret_t

    # ── Total P&L and capital update ─────────────────────────────────────────
    total_pnl_t     <- strat_pnl_t + tbill_pnl_t
    capital_running <- capital_running + total_pnl_t
    maintenance_margin_call_t <- is_open &&
      capital_running < maintenance_margin_t
    stress_limit_breach_t <- is_open &&
      stress_margin_t > MAX_STRESS_MARGIN_UTILIZATION * capital_running
    stress_utilization_end_t <- if (capital_running > 0) {
      stress_margin_t / capital_running
    } else if (is_open) {
      Inf
    } else {
      0
    }

    # ── Store results ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    strategy_pnl_gross[t]    <- strat_pnl_gross_t
    transaction_cost[t]      <- transaction_cost_t
    strategy_pnl[t]          <- strat_pnl_t
    tbill_pnl[t]             <- tbill_pnl_t
    total_pnl[t]             <- total_pnl_t
    capital[t]               <- capital_running
    capital_start_week_vec[t]<- capital_start_week_t
    idle_cash_vec[t]         <- idle_cash_t
    margin_posted_vec[t]     <- margin_t
    margin_face_value_vec[t] <- margin_face_value_t
    maintenance_margin_vec[t]<- maintenance_margin_t
    stress_margin_vec[t]     <- stress_margin_t
    stress_margin_limit_vec[t] <- stress_margin_limit_t
    stress_util_start_vec[t] <- stress_utilization_start_t
    stress_util_end_vec[t]   <- stress_utilization_end_t
    margin_capacity_vec[t]   <- margin_capacity_t
    desired_contracts_vec[t] <- desired_contracts_t
    tbill_rate_weekly[t]     <- weekly_ret_t
    n_contracts_vec[t]       <- current_contracts_held
    held_pos_CL1[t]          <- sign(curr_signed_qty_CL1)
    held_pos_CL17[t]         <- sign(curr_signed_qty_CL17)
    contracts_traded_CL1[t]  <- trade_qty_CL1
    contracts_traded_CL17[t] <- trade_qty_CL17
    maintenance_margin_call[t] <- maintenance_margin_call_t
    stress_limit_breach[t]   <- stress_limit_breach_t
    margin_cap_binding[t]    <- margin_cap_binding_t
    margin_entry_cap[t]      <- margin_entry_cap_t
    margin_forced_reduction[t] <- margin_forced_reduction_t
    margin_action[t]         <- margin_action_t
    held_und_CL1[t]          <- target_ticker_CL1
    held_und_CL17[t]         <- target_ticker_CL17
    held_price_prev_CL1[t]   <- curr_price_prev_CL1
    held_price_prev_CL17[t]  <- curr_price_prev_CL17
    held_price_curr_CL1[t]   <- curr_price_now_CL1
    held_price_curr_CL17[t]  <- curr_price_now_CL17
    exec_roll_CL1[t]         <- exec_roll_CL1_t
    exec_roll_CL17[t]        <- exec_roll_CL17_t
    roll_reason_CL1[t]       <- roll_reason_CL1_t
    roll_reason_CL17[t]      <- roll_reason_CL17_t

    trade_change_type[t] <- dplyr::case_when(
      prev_signed_qty_CL1 == 0L && curr_signed_qty_CL1 != 0L ~ "entry",
      prev_signed_qty_CL1 != 0L && curr_signed_qty_CL1 == 0L ~ "exit",
      prev_signed_qty_CL1 * curr_signed_qty_CL1 < 0L ~ "flip",
      abs(curr_signed_qty_CL1) > abs(prev_signed_qty_CL1) ~ "upsize",
      abs(curr_signed_qty_CL1) < abs(prev_signed_qty_CL1) ~ "downsize",
      prev_signed_qty_CL1 == curr_signed_qty_CL1 ~ "no_position_change",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )

    any_exec_roll <- exec_roll_CL1_t || exec_roll_CL17_t
    any_trade_change <- trade_change_type[t] != "no_position_change"
    cost_event_type[t] <- dplyr::case_when(
      any_exec_roll && any_trade_change ~ "roll_plus_trade_change",
      any_exec_roll ~ "roll_only",
      any_trade_change ~ "trade_change_only",
      TRUE ~ "none"
    )

    held_ticker_prev_CL1  <- target_ticker_CL1
    held_ticker_prev_CL17 <- target_ticker_CL17
  }

  dplyr::tibble(
    date                = trade_dates,
    pos_CL1             = pos_CL1,
    pos_CL17            = pos_CL17,
    held_pos_CL1        = held_pos_CL1,
    held_pos_CL17       = held_pos_CL17,
    price_CL1           = price_CL1_t,
    price_CL17          = price_CL17_t,
    strategy_pnl_gross  = round(strategy_pnl_gross,    2),
    transaction_cost    = round(transaction_cost,      2),
    strategy_pnl        = round(strategy_pnl,        2),
    capital_start_week  = round(capital_start_week_vec, 2),
    margin_posted       = margin_posted_vec,
    maintenance_margin_required = maintenance_margin_vec,
    stress_margin_required = stress_margin_vec,
    stress_margin_limit = round(stress_margin_limit_vec, 2),
    stress_margin_utilization_start = round(stress_util_start_vec, 8),
    stress_margin_utilization_end = round(stress_util_end_vec, 8),
    margin_face_value   = round(margin_face_value_vec, 2),
    idle_cash           = round(idle_cash_vec,         2),
    tbill_rate_weekly   = round(tbill_rate_weekly,     8),
    tbill_pnl           = round(tbill_pnl,             2),
    total_pnl           = round(total_pnl,             2),
    capital             = round(capital,               2),
    roll_CL1            = roll_CL1_t,
    roll_CL17           = roll_CL17_t,
    generic_und_CL1     = generic_und_CL1,
    generic_und_CL17    = generic_und_CL17,
    generic_ltd_CL1     = ltd_CL1_t,
    generic_ltd_CL17    = ltd_CL17_t,
    held_und_CL1        = held_und_CL1,
    held_und_CL17       = held_und_CL17,
    held_price_prev_CL1 = held_price_prev_CL1,
    held_price_prev_CL17= held_price_prev_CL17,
    held_price_curr_CL1 = held_price_curr_CL1,
    held_price_curr_CL17= held_price_curr_CL17,
    exec_roll_CL1       = exec_roll_CL1,
    exec_roll_CL17      = exec_roll_CL17,
    roll_reason_CL1     = roll_reason_CL1,
    roll_reason_CL17    = roll_reason_CL17,
    block_id            = block_id,
    n_contracts         = n_contracts_vec,
    desired_contracts_before_margin = desired_contracts_vec,
    margin_capacity_spreads = margin_capacity_vec,
    contracts_traded_CL1  = contracts_traded_CL1,
    contracts_traded_CL17 = contracts_traded_CL17,
    trade_change_type   = trade_change_type,
    cost_event_type     = cost_event_type,
    maintenance_margin_call = maintenance_margin_call,
    stress_limit_breach = stress_limit_breach,
    margin_cap_binding  = margin_cap_binding,
    margin_entry_cap    = margin_entry_cap,
    margin_forced_reduction = margin_forced_reduction,
    margin_action       = margin_action
  )
}

```

## Step 7: Outer Rebalancing Loop

This section assembles the full backtest by iterating over every block
in the schedule. For each block it estimates parameters on the expanding
training window, runs the forward Kalman filter over the trading year,
generates signals, computes P&L, and carries the filter state and open
position forward into the next block. All per-block results are
concatenated into a single results data frame covering the full trading
period.

```{r step7, include=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=c(file.info(PATH_FUTURES)$mtime, file.info(PATH_TBILL)$mtime)}

# After the first run, this annual estimation is stored as a cache in results/.
# It makes repeated rendering practical. Removing the file below forces
# the complete raw-data estimation and recreates the same object from scratch.
REFERENCE_CACHE <- file.path(PATH_OUTPUT, "ss2000_raw_reference_cache.rds")

if (file.exists(REFERENCE_CACHE)) {
  cached_reference <- readRDS(REFERENCE_CACHE)
  required_cache_objects <- c("results_df", "theta_list", "schedule")
  if (!all(required_cache_objects %in% names(cached_reference))) {
    stop("The local SS2000 reference cache is incomplete")
  }

  results_df <- cached_reference$results_df # Weekly raw signal and execution ledger.
  theta_list <- cached_reference$theta_list # Annual parameter estimates.
  schedule <- cached_reference$schedule     # Expanding train/trade windows.
} else {

#############################################################################
# STEP 7.0 — Initialise storage
#############################################################################

n_blocks     <- nrow(schedule)

# Per-block results stored in a list, concatenated at the end
results_list  <- vector("list", n_blocks)
theta_list    <- vector("list", n_blocks)   # estimated theta_hat per block

# Carry the actual position and held-underlying state across calendar blocks.
# The latent-state prior is not carried under stale parameters: every annual
# theta refilters its complete training sample and supplies its own prediction.
pos_carry_CL1     <- 0L
held_und_carry_CL1  <- NA_character_
held_und_carry_CL17 <- NA_character_

message("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════")
message("Starting outer rebalancing loop — ", n_blocks, " blocks")
message("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════")

#############################################################################
# STEP 7.1 — Main loop
#############################################################################

for (k in seq_len(n_blocks)) {

  blk <- schedule[k, ]
  message("\n── Block ", k, " of ", n_blocks,
          " | Trading year: ", blk$trading_year, " ──")

  # ── 1. Subset training and trading windows ─────────────────────────────────
  train_idx  <- blk$train_start_idx:blk$train_end_idx
  trade_idx  <- blk$trade_start_idx:blk$trade_end_idx

  Y_train    <- Y[,   train_idx, drop = FALSE]
  Tau_train  <- Tau[, train_idx, drop = FALSE]

  Y_trade    <- Y[,   trade_idx, drop = FALSE]
  Tau_trade  <- Tau[, trade_idx, drop = FALSE]

  trade_dates   <- obs_dates[trade_idx]
  price_CL1_t   <- price_CL1[trade_idx]
  price_CL17_t  <- price_CL17[trade_idx]
  und_CL1_t     <- und_CL1[trade_idx]
  und_CL17_t    <- und_CL17[trade_idx]
  ltd_CL1_t     <- ltd_CL1[trade_idx]
  ltd_CL17_t    <- ltd_CL17[trade_idx]
  px_all_t      <- PX_ALL[trade_idx,  , drop = FALSE]
  und_all_t     <- UND_ALL[trade_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  ltd_all_t     <- LTD_ALL[trade_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  dtb3_t        <- dtb3[trade_idx]
  roll_CL1_t    <- roll_CL1[trade_idx]
  roll_CL17_t   <- roll_CL17[trade_idx]
  prev_idx_k    <- min(trade_idx) - 1L
  px_prev_row_k <- PX_ALL[prev_idx_k,  , drop = TRUE]
  und_prev_row_k<- UND_ALL[prev_idx_k, , drop = TRUE]
  ltd_prev_row_k<- LTD_ALL[prev_idx_k, , drop = TRUE]

  # ── 2. Estimate parameters on training window ──────────────────────────────
  theta_hat_k <- estimate_ss(
    Y_train   = Y_train,
    Tau_train = Tau_train,
    Delta_t   = DELTA_T,
    n_starts  = N_STARTS,
    block_id  = k
  )
  theta_list[[k]] <- theta_hat_k

  # ── 3. Use this annual model's one-step-ahead trading prior ────────────────
  # December's posterior contains the complete expanding training information.
  # FKF has already propagated it through one weekly SS2000 transition, including
  # process noise, so these objects correspond to the first January observation.
  m0_k <- theta_hat_k$at_trade_start
  P0_k <- theta_hat_k$Pt_trade_start
  message("  [Block ", k, "] Using training filter's one-step-ahead prior")
  message("  [Block ", k, "] Prior: chi = ", round(m0_k[1], 4),
          "  xi = ", round(m0_k[2], 4))

  # ── 4. Run forward Kalman filter over trading year ─────────────────────────
  kf_k <- run_forward_kf(
    theta_hat = theta_hat_k,
    Y_trade   = Y_trade,
    Tau_trade = Tau_trade,
    Delta_t   = DELTA_T,
    m0_init   = m0_k,
    P0_init   = P0_k,
    block_id  = k
  )

  # ── 5. Generate the boundary position and trading-year signals ─────────────
  # The prepended December posterior uses only training data. Its signal is held
  # over the first January return. January's posterior then controls week two.
  sig_with_boundary <- generate_signals(
    chi_vec    = c(theta_hat_k$att_train_end[1L], kf_k$chi_vec),
    theta_hat  = theta_hat_k,
    block_id   = k,
    initial_pos = pos_carry_CL1
  )
  pos_start_k <- sig_with_boundary$pos_CL1[1L]
  sig_k <- list(
    z_vec     = sig_with_boundary$z_vec[-1L],
    pos_CL1   = sig_with_boundary$pos_CL1[-1L],
    pos_CL17  = sig_with_boundary$pos_CL17[-1L],
    trade_log = sig_with_boundary$trade_log,
    state_end = sig_with_boundary$state_end
  )

  # ── 6. Compute P&L ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Starting capital: $1M for block 1, ending capital of prior block thereafter
  capital_start_k <- if (k == 1L) {
    INITIAL_CAPITAL
  } else {
    tail(results_list[[k - 1L]]$capital, 1L)
  }

  # ── Compute entry-date EMA level dispersion from the executable spread ─────
  # The sizing signal updates only when a new trade is entered. For each
  # trading week we precompute the EW spread-level SD observable from the
  # tradeable spread history through t-1.
  hist_idx   <- seq_len(max(trade_idx))
  spread_hist <- build_execution_spread_levels(
    index_seq = hist_idx,
    obs_dates_vec = obs_dates,
    und_CL1_vec = und_CL1,
    und_CL17_vec = und_CL17,
    px_all_mat = PX_ALL,
    und_all_mat = UND_ALL,
    ltd_all_mat = LTD_ALL
  )
  entry_level_sd_hist <- build_entry_ema_level_sd_series(
    spread_levels = spread_hist,
    half_life = EMA_LEVEL_HALF_LIFE
  )
  entry_level_sd_k <- entry_level_sd_hist[trade_idx]

  entry_level_sd_preview <- entry_level_sd_k[which(is.finite(entry_level_sd_k))[1L]]
  n_contracts_expected <- if (is.finite(entry_level_sd_preview) && entry_level_sd_preview > 0) {
    max(N_CONTRACTS_MIN, min(N_CONTRACTS_MAX,
      as.integer(round((RANGE_BUDGET_PCT * capital_start_k) /
                       (entry_level_sd_preview * CONTRACT_SIZE)))))
  } else { 25L }

  message("  [Block ", k, "] Capital: $", format(round(capital_start_k), big.mark = ","),
          " | first entry EMA level SD: $", round(entry_level_sd_preview, 2), "/bbl",
          " | expected contracts at first entry: ", n_contracts_expected)

  # Carry prior trade size across the year boundary so an already-open
  # position starts the new year at its carried size. Open trades are not
  # resized just because the calendar year changes.
  n_contracts_carry_k <- if (k == 1L) 0L else tail(results_list[[k - 1L]]$n_contracts, 1L)

  pnl_k <- compute_pnl(
      pos_CL1          = sig_k$pos_CL1,
      pos_CL17         = sig_k$pos_CL17,
      price_CL1_t      = price_CL1_t,
      price_CL17_t     = price_CL17_t,
      und_CL1_t        = und_CL1_t,
      und_CL17_t       = und_CL17_t,
      ltd_CL1_t        = ltd_CL1_t,
      ltd_CL17_t       = ltd_CL17_t,
      px_all_t         = px_all_t,
      und_all_t        = und_all_t,
      ltd_all_t        = ltd_all_t,
      dtb3_t           = dtb3_t,
      roll_CL1_t       = roll_CL1_t,
      roll_CL17_t      = roll_CL17_t,
      capital_start    = capital_start_k,
      trade_dates      = trade_dates,
      block_id         = k,
      pos_start_CL1    = pos_start_k,
      pos_prev_CL1     = pos_carry_CL1,
      px_prev_row      = px_prev_row_k,
      und_prev_row     = und_prev_row_k,
      ltd_prev_row     = ltd_prev_row_k,
      held_und_prev_CL1 = held_und_carry_CL1,
      held_und_prev_CL17 = held_und_carry_CL17,
      n_contracts      = n_contracts_carry_k,
      entry_level_sd_t = entry_level_sd_k
    )
  
  
  # ── 7. Store results ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  results_list[[k]] <- pnl_k %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      trading_year     = blk$trading_year,
      z_score          = sig_k$z_vec,
      chi              = kf_k$chi_vec,
      xi               = kf_k$xi_vec,
      kappa            = theta_hat_k$kappa,
      sigma_chi        = theta_hat_k$sigma_chi,
      sigma_xi         = theta_hat_k$sigma_xi,
      spread_level_sd  = entry_level_sd_k,
      boundary_z_score = c(sig_with_boundary$z_vec[1L],
                           rep(NA_real_, nrow(pnl_k) - 1L)),
      boundary_pos_before = c(pos_carry_CL1,
                              rep(NA_integer_, nrow(pnl_k) - 1L)),
      boundary_pos_start = c(pos_start_k,
                             rep(NA_integer_, nrow(pnl_k) - 1L))
    )

  # ── 8. Carry the actual final-week holding into the next boundary decision ─
  pos_carry_CL1     <- tail(pnl_k$held_pos_CL1, 1L)
  held_und_carry_CL1  <- tail(pnl_k$held_und_CL1, 1L)
  held_und_carry_CL17 <- tail(pnl_k$held_und_CL17, 1L)

  message("  [Block ", k, "] Year complete — ",
          "strategy P&L net: $", format(round(sum(pnl_k$strategy_pnl), 0),
                                    big.mark = ","),
          " | costs: $", format(round(sum(pnl_k$transaction_cost), 0),
                                big.mark = ","),
          " | T-bill P&L: $", format(round(sum(pnl_k$tbill_pnl), 0),
                                     big.mark = ","),
          " | Capital: $", format(round(tail(pnl_k$capital, 1L), 0),
                                  big.mark = ","))
}

message("\n═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════")
message("Loop complete")
message("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════")

#############################################################################
# STEP 7.2 — Concatenate all blocks into a single results data frame
#############################################################################

results_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(results_list)

stopifnot(nrow(results_df) == sum(schedule$n_trade_weeks))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(results_df$capital)))
stopifnot(all(results_df$capital > 0))

# The reference pass is saved only as a local cache for faster re-knitting.
# Every input needed to rebuild it is defined in this notebook.
saveRDS(
  list(results_df = results_df, theta_list = theta_list, schedule = schedule),
  REFERENCE_CACHE
)

} # End raw rebuild / local-cache branch.

```

## Step 8: Strategy Research and Final Backtest

The model output above is now treated as a fixed signal and execution
reference. The remainder of the notebook changes only the trading rule,
position size and implementation assumptions described explicitly below.

### 8.1 Build the common signal and execution reference

The raw directional benchmark is always invested. This means its gross P&L
can be divided by its signed contract holding to recover the tradable weekly
P&L of one long CL1 / short CL17 spread. Every strategy below uses this same
return series, roll schedule and decision timing.

```{r research-reference, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Work with a plain data frame because the research functions below use both
# base-R indexing and dplyr summaries.
full_ref <- as.data.frame(results_df)
full_ref$date <- as.Date(full_ref$date)

# The raw signal should always hold a non-zero integer quantity. Without this
# property, division could not recover the one-spread gross return exactly.
signed_reference_quantity <- full_ref$held_pos_CL1 * full_ref$n_contracts
if (any(signed_reference_quantity == 0L)) {
  stop("The raw-signal reference unexpectedly contains a flat week")
}

# Gross P&L is reconstructed before any transaction cost or collateral return.
full_ref$long_spread_unit_gross <-
  full_ref$strategy_pnl_gross / signed_reference_quantity

# Rebuild spread-level dispersion for the two half-life sensitivities as well
# as the 26-week primary rule. Each value uses observations only through t-1.
execution_spread_full <- build_execution_spread_levels(
  index_seq = seq_along(obs_dates),
  obs_dates_vec = obs_dates,
  und_CL1_vec = und_CL1,
  und_CL17_vec = und_CL17,
  px_all_mat = PX_ALL,
  und_all_mat = UND_ALL,
  ltd_all_mat = LTD_ALL
)

spread_sd_full <- lapply(c(`13` = 13L, `26` = 26L, `52` = 52L), function(half_life) {
  build_entry_ema_level_sd_series(execution_spread_full, half_life = half_life)
})

trade_rows <- match(full_ref$date, obs_dates) # Align live weeks to the full history.
if (anyNA(trade_rows)) stop("Live strategy dates are absent from the raw data")

full_ref$spread_level_sd_13 <- spread_sd_full[["13"]][trade_rows]
full_ref$spread_level_sd_26 <- spread_sd_full[["26"]][trade_rows]
full_ref$spread_level_sd_52 <- spread_sd_full[["52"]][trade_rows]

# The independently rebuilt 26-week path must reproduce the value generated
# inside the annual loop. This catches accidental changes in lagging or rolls.
ema_26_error <- max(
  abs(full_ref$spread_level_sd_26 - full_ref$spread_level_sd),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
if (ema_26_error > 1e-10) {
  stop("The 26-week spread dispersion did not reconstruct exactly")
}

# A position held in week t is decided at the previous weekly close. At the
# first week of a year, the correctly propagated December posterior supplies
# the decision instead of a newly observed January value.
build_decision_z <- function(data) {
  is_year_start <- c(TRUE, diff(data$trading_year) != 0)
  z_decision <- numeric(nrow(data))
  z_decision[is_year_start] <- data$boundary_z_score[is_year_start]
  z_decision[!is_year_start] <- data$z_score[which(!is_year_start) - 1L]

  if (any(!is.finite(z_decision))) stop("Decision z-score contains invalid values")
  z_decision
}

full_ref$decision_z <- build_decision_z(full_ref)

# Calibration is the only period allowed to influence the rule selection.
CALIBRATION_END <- as.Date("2016-12-31")
OOS_START <- as.Date("2017-01-01")
calibration_ref <- full_ref[full_ref$date <= CALIBRATION_END, , drop = FALSE]
if (max(calibration_ref$date) > CALIBRATION_END) stop("Calibration firewall failed")

# This compact table records the choices that remain fixed throughout.
design_table <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Traded spread", "Signal estimation", "Initial history", "Calibration",
    "Out-of-sample period", "Position ratio", "Primary sizing", "Costs",
    "Stress-margin limit"
  ),
  Choice = c(
    "Long/short CL1 against CL17", "Annual expanding SS2000 filter",
    "1990-1999", "2000-2016", "2017-2025", "1:1 integer contracts",
    "Fixed at entry; 26-week half-life spread-level dispersion",
    "$12.50 CL1 and $22.50 CL17 per contract-side",
    "$15,000 per spread, capped at 80% of start-of-week equity"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  design_table,
  caption = "Fixed research and implementation choices",
  align = c("l", "l")
)

```

### 8.2 Trading rules and portfolio accounting
The filtered short-term factor is standardized by the empirical standard deviation 
of filtered \(\chi\) estimated over the corresponding expanding training sample. 
The theoretical stationary standard deviation is used only as a fallback when the 
empirical normalizer is unavailable. A negative z-score therefore supports a long 
spread, while a positive z-score supports a short spread. Baseline A trades
that direction with one spread. Baseline B uses the same direction but applies
the final fixed-at-entry sizing rule.

The threshold strategy enters only when the deviation is large enough, exits
after partial convergence, and can impose a maximum holding period. A timed-out
direction cannot immediately re-enter until the signal first moves back inside
its entry boundary.

```{r strategy-functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Return the raw SS2000 direction. sign(z) and sign(chi) are identical because
# the z-score denominator is strictly positive.
generate_signal_only <- function(z_decision) {
  position <- integer(length(z_decision))
  current_position <- 0L

  for (i in seq_along(z_decision)) {
    if (is.finite(z_decision[i])) current_position <- as.integer(-sign(z_decision[i]))
    position[i] <- current_position # The close-t decision is held over week t+1.
  }

  position
}

# Apply symmetric entry and convergence boundaries with an optional time stop.
generate_threshold_positions <- function(z_decision, entry, exit, time_stop) {
  if (!is.finite(entry) || entry <= 0) stop("Entry must be positive")
  if (!is.finite(exit) || exit < 0 || exit >= entry) {
    stop("Exit must satisfy 0 <= exit < entry")
  }
  if (!is.infinite(time_stop) &&
      (!is.finite(time_stop) || time_stop < 1 || time_stop != floor(time_stop))) {
    stop("Time stop must be Inf or a positive integer")
  }

  position <- integer(length(z_decision))
  age <- integer(length(z_decision))
  exit_reason <- rep("none", length(z_decision))
  current_position <- 0L
  current_age <- 0L
  blocked_direction <- 0L

  for (i in seq_along(z_decision)) {
    z <- z_decision[i]

    # A time-stopped trade must observe a fresh boundary crossing before the
    # same direction can be opened again.
    if (blocked_direction == 1L && z > -entry) blocked_direction <- 0L
    if (blocked_direction == -1L && z < entry) blocked_direction <- 0L

    if (current_position == 0L) {
      if (z <= -entry && blocked_direction != 1L) {
        current_position <- 1L # Negative short-term factor: long the spread.
        current_age <- 1L
      } else if (z >= entry && blocked_direction != -1L) {
        current_position <- -1L # Positive short-term factor: short the spread.
        current_age <- 1L
      } else {
        current_age <- 0L
      }
    } else {
      timed_out <- is.finite(time_stop) && current_age >= time_stop
      converged <- (current_position == 1L && z >= -exit) ||
        (current_position == -1L && z <= exit)

      if (timed_out || converged) {
        old_direction <- current_position
        exit_reason[i] <- if (timed_out) "time_stop" else "convergence"
        current_position <- 0L
        current_age <- 0L

        if (timed_out) blocked_direction <- old_direction

        # A move through the opposite entry boundary is a genuine same-date
        # reversal, so it is allowed without forcing an artificial flat week.
        if (z <= -entry && blocked_direction != 1L) {
          current_position <- 1L
          current_age <- 1L
          exit_reason[i] <- paste0(exit_reason[i], "+flip")
        } else if (z >= entry && blocked_direction != -1L) {
          current_position <- -1L
          current_age <- 1L
          exit_reason[i] <- paste0(exit_reason[i], "+flip")
        }
      } else {
        current_age <- current_age + 1L
      }
    }

    position[i] <- current_position
    age[i] <- current_age
  }

  data.frame(position = position, age = age, exit_reason = exit_reason)
}

# A zero lag is used for positions and quantities before the first live week.
lag_zero <- function(x) c(0, head(x, -1L))

# Simulate one strategy with a common execution, cost, collateral and margin
# engine. Position is the holding during each weekly return interval.
simulate_portfolio <- function(data, position, sizing_mode = c("unit", "fixed_entry", "weekly_resize"),
                               ema_half_life = 26L,
                               cost_cl1 = BASE_COST_CL1,
                               cost_cl17 = BASE_COST_CL17) {
  sizing_mode <- match.arg(sizing_mode)
  if (length(position) != nrow(data)) stop("Position length mismatch")
  if (!ema_half_life %in% c(13L, 26L, 52L)) stop("Unsupported EMA half-life")

  sd_column <- paste0("spread_level_sd_", ema_half_life)
  if (!sd_column %in% names(data)) stop("Missing sizing column: ", sd_column)

  n <- nrow(data)
  contracts <- integer(n)
  desired_contracts <- integer(n)
  gross_pnl <- numeric(n)
  transaction_cost <- numeric(n)
  net_pnl <- numeric(n)
  capital_start <- numeric(n)
  tbill_pnl <- numeric(n)
  capital_end <- numeric(n)
  margin_posted <- numeric(n)
  stress_margin <- numeric(n)
  stress_utilization <- numeric(n)
  margin_cap_binding <- logical(n)
  maintenance_call <- logical(n)
  quantity_cl1 <- numeric(n)
  quantity_cl17 <- numeric(n)

  capital <- INITIAL_CAPITAL
  current_contracts <- 0L

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    capital_start[i] <- capital
    previous_position <- if (i == 1L) 0L else position[i - 1L]
    previous_contracts <- if (i == 1L) 0L else contracts[i - 1L]
    is_new_trade <- position[i] != 0L &&
      (previous_position == 0L || previous_position != position[i])

    if (position[i] == 0L) {
      current_contracts <- 0L
    } else if (sizing_mode == "unit") {
      current_contracts <- 1L
    } else if (is_new_trade || sizing_mode == "weekly_resize") {
      spread_sd <- data[[sd_column]][i] # Already lagged, so no current-week data enter.
      if (!is.finite(spread_sd) || spread_sd <= 0) {
        stop("Spread-level dispersion unavailable on ", data$date[i])
      }

      raw_contracts <- (RANGE_BUDGET_PCT * capital) /
        (spread_sd * CONTRACT_SIZE)
      current_contracts <- max(
        N_CONTRACTS_MIN,
        min(N_CONTRACTS_MAX, as.integer(round(raw_contracts)))
      )
    }

    desired_contracts[i] <- if (position[i] == 0L) 0L else current_contracts

    # Margin is a feasibility cap, not a second sizing target. It can reduce
    # the desired quantity but can never increase it.
    margin_capacity <- max(0L, as.integer(floor(
      MAX_STRESS_MARGIN_UTILIZATION * capital / STRESS_MARGIN_PER_SPREAD
    )))
    if (current_contracts > margin_capacity) {
      margin_cap_binding[i] <- TRUE
      current_contracts <- margin_capacity
    }
    if (position[i] != 0L && current_contracts == 0L) {
      stop("Margin capacity blocked a signalled trade")
    }

    contracts[i] <- if (position[i] == 0L) 0L else current_contracts

    signed_now_cl1 <- position[i] * contracts[i]
    signed_previous_cl1 <- previous_position * previous_contracts
    signed_now_cl17 <- -signed_now_cl1
    signed_previous_cl17 <- -signed_previous_cl1

    # A held leg that rolls closes the old contract and opens the new one. A
    # normal entry, exit or resize pays only for the net quantity change.
    quantity_cl1[i] <- if (signed_previous_cl1 != 0L && signed_now_cl1 != 0L &&
                           data$exec_roll_CL1[i]) {
      abs(signed_previous_cl1) + abs(signed_now_cl1)
    } else {
      abs(signed_now_cl1 - signed_previous_cl1)
    }
    quantity_cl17[i] <- if (signed_previous_cl17 != 0L && signed_now_cl17 != 0L &&
                            data$exec_roll_CL17[i]) {
      abs(signed_previous_cl17) + abs(signed_now_cl17)
    } else {
      abs(signed_now_cl17 - signed_previous_cl17)
    }

    gross_pnl[i] <- signed_now_cl1 * data$long_spread_unit_gross[i]
    transaction_cost[i] <- quantity_cl1[i] * cost_cl1 +
      quantity_cl17[i] * cost_cl17
    net_pnl[i] <- gross_pnl[i] - transaction_cost[i]

    margin_posted[i] <- contracts[i] * INITIAL_MARGIN_PER_SPREAD
    stress_margin[i] <- contracts[i] * STRESS_MARGIN_PER_SPREAD
    stress_utilization[i] <- if (capital > 0) stress_margin[i] / capital else Inf
    if (stress_utilization[i] > MAX_STRESS_MARGIN_UTILIZATION + 1e-12) {
      stop("Stress-margin limit was exceeded")
    }

    # Only cash not posted as initial margin earns the observed T-bill return.
    # The 0.5% collateral haircut is checked as a solvency constraint.
    if (capital < margin_posted[i] / (1 - TBILL_HAIRCUT)) {
      stop("Capital cannot cover the haircutted collateral")
    }
    idle_cash <- max(capital - margin_posted[i], 0)
    tbill_pnl[i] <- idle_cash * data$tbill_rate_weekly[i]

    capital <- capital + net_pnl[i] + tbill_pnl[i]
    capital_end[i] <- capital
    maintenance_call[i] <- contracts[i] > 0L &&
      capital < contracts[i] * MAINTENANCE_MARGIN_PER_SPREAD
  }

  data.frame(
    date = data$date,
    trading_year = data$trading_year,
    z_score = data$z_score,
    decision_z = data$decision_z,
    position = as.integer(position),
    contracts = contracts,
    desired_contracts = desired_contracts,
    gross_pnl = gross_pnl,
    transaction_cost = transaction_cost,
    net_pnl = net_pnl,
    quantity_cl1 = quantity_cl1,
    quantity_cl17 = quantity_cl17,
    capital_start = capital_start,
    tbill_rate_weekly = data$tbill_rate_weekly,
    tbill_pnl = tbill_pnl,
    capital_end = capital_end,
    margin_posted = margin_posted,
    stress_margin = stress_margin,
    stress_utilization = stress_utilization,
    margin_cap_binding = margin_cap_binding,
    maintenance_call = maintenance_call,
    exec_roll_cl1 = data$exec_roll_CL1,
    exec_roll_cl17 = data$exec_roll_CL17,
    sizing_mode = sizing_mode,
    ema_half_life = ema_half_life
  )
}

```

```{r reporting-functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Allocate entry, roll and exit costs to the trade that generated them. Exit
# costs occur on the first flat week, so they must be assigned back to the
# trade that ended rather than being dropped from the trade-level report.
build_trade_log <- function(simulation) {
  n <- nrow(simulation)
  previous_position <- lag_zero(simulation$position)
  is_entry <- simulation$position != 0L &
    (previous_position == 0L | previous_position != simulation$position)

  trade_id <- integer(n)
  current_id <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (is_entry[i]) current_id <- current_id + 1L
    if (simulation$position[i] != 0L) trade_id[i] <- current_id
  }
  if (current_id == 0L) return(data.frame())

  gross_by_trade <- numeric(current_id)
  cost_by_trade <- numeric(current_id)

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (trade_id[i] > 0L) {
      gross_by_trade[trade_id[i]] <- gross_by_trade[trade_id[i]] +
        simulation$gross_pnl[i]
    }
    if (simulation$transaction_cost[i] == 0) next

    previous_id <- if (i == 1L) 0L else trade_id[i - 1L]
    current_id_i <- trade_id[i]
    previous_pos <- if (i == 1L) 0L else simulation$position[i - 1L]
    current_pos <- simulation$position[i]

    if (previous_pos == 0L && current_pos != 0L) {
      cost_by_trade[current_id_i] <- cost_by_trade[current_id_i] +
        simulation$transaction_cost[i]
    } else if (previous_pos != 0L && current_pos == 0L) {
      cost_by_trade[previous_id] <- cost_by_trade[previous_id] +
        simulation$transaction_cost[i]
    } else if (previous_pos != 0L && current_pos != 0L && previous_pos != current_pos) {
      # A direct flip closes one trade and opens the next, so the combined
      # execution cost is split equally between the two episodes.
      cost_by_trade[previous_id] <- cost_by_trade[previous_id] +
        simulation$transaction_cost[i] / 2
      cost_by_trade[current_id_i] <- cost_by_trade[current_id_i] +
        simulation$transaction_cost[i] / 2
    } else if (current_id_i > 0L) {
      cost_by_trade[current_id_i] <- cost_by_trade[current_id_i] +
        simulation$transaction_cost[i]
    }
  }

  records <- lapply(seq_len(current_id), function(id) {
    holding_rows <- which(trade_id == id)
    first_row <- min(holding_rows)
    last_row <- max(holding_rows)
    exit_row <- if (last_row < n &&
                    simulation$position[last_row + 1L] != simulation$position[last_row]) {
      last_row + 1L
    } else {
      NA_integer_
    }

    data.frame(
      trade_id = id,
      direction = if (simulation$position[first_row] == 1L) "long" else "short",
      entry_date = simulation$date[first_row],
      last_holding_date = simulation$date[last_row],
      exit_execution_date = if (is.na(exit_row)) as.Date(NA) else simulation$date[exit_row],
      completed = !is.na(exit_row),
      holding_weeks = length(holding_rows),
      contracts_entry = simulation$contracts[first_row],
      average_contracts = mean(simulation$contracts[holding_rows]),
      gross_pnl = gross_by_trade[id],
      transaction_cost = cost_by_trade[id],
      net_pnl = gross_by_trade[id] - cost_by_trade[id]
    )
  })

  trade_log <- do.call(rbind, records)

  # The trade report is accepted only if it reconciles to the weekly ledger.
  if (abs(sum(trade_log$gross_pnl) - sum(simulation$gross_pnl)) > 1e-8 ||
      abs(sum(trade_log$transaction_cost) - sum(simulation$transaction_cost)) > 1e-8 ||
      abs(sum(trade_log$net_pnl) - sum(simulation$net_pnl)) > 1e-8) {
    stop("Trade log does not reconcile to the weekly portfolio ledger")
  }

  trade_log
}

# Close a continuously active benchmark after the final weekly return so it
# cannot avoid the cost of eventually liquidating both legs.
add_terminal_liquidation <- function(simulation, cost_cl1, cost_cl17) {
  last_row <- nrow(simulation)
  closing_contracts <- simulation$contracts[last_row]
  simulation$terminal_liquidation_qty <- 0L
  if (closing_contracts == 0L) return(simulation)

  liquidation_cost <- closing_contracts * (cost_cl1 + cost_cl17)
  simulation$terminal_liquidation_qty[last_row] <- closing_contracts
  simulation$quantity_cl1[last_row] <- simulation$quantity_cl1[last_row] + closing_contracts
  simulation$quantity_cl17[last_row] <- simulation$quantity_cl17[last_row] + closing_contracts
  simulation$transaction_cost[last_row] <-
    simulation$transaction_cost[last_row] + liquidation_cost
  simulation$net_pnl[last_row] <- simulation$net_pnl[last_row] - liquidation_cost
  simulation$capital_end[last_row] <- simulation$capital_end[last_row] - liquidation_cost
  simulation
}

# The terminal close belongs to the final trade episode for reconciliation.
build_liquidated_trade_log <- function(simulation) {
  trade_log <- build_trade_log(simulation)
  if (nrow(trade_log) > 0L && tail(simulation$terminal_liquidation_qty, 1L) > 0L) {
    final_trade <- nrow(trade_log)
    trade_log$completed[final_trade] <- TRUE
    trade_log$exit_execution_date[final_trade] <- max(simulation$date)
  }
  trade_log
}

# Summarise a complete simulation without including passive T-bill income in
# the strategy's information ratio or futures drawdown.
summarize_simulation <- function(simulation, trade_log) {
  weekly_return <- simulation$net_pnl / simulation$capital_start
  futures_wealth <- INITIAL_CAPITAL + cumsum(simulation$net_pnl)
  drawdown <- futures_wealth / cummax(c(INITIAL_CAPITAL, futures_wealth))[-1L] - 1
  account_pnl <- simulation$net_pnl + simulation$tbill_pnl
  account_return <- account_pnl / simulation$capital_start
  account_excess_return <- account_return - simulation$tbill_rate_weekly
  account_peak <- cummax(c(INITIAL_CAPITAL, simulation$capital_end))[-1L]
  account_drawdown <- simulation$capital_end / account_peak - 1
  period_years <- nrow(simulation) / 52
  annual <- aggregate(
    cbind(gross_pnl, transaction_cost, net_pnl) ~ trading_year,
    data = simulation,
    FUN = sum
  )

  total_net <- sum(simulation$net_pnl)
  best_trade <- if (nrow(trade_log)) max(trade_log$net_pnl) else NA_real_
  best_year <- max(annual$net_pnl)

  data.frame(
    gross_pnl = sum(simulation$gross_pnl),
    transaction_cost = sum(simulation$transaction_cost),
    net_futures_pnl = total_net,
    total_account_pnl = sum(account_pnl),
    net_futures_return_on_start_pct =
      100 * total_net / INITIAL_CAPITAL,
    annualized_mean_futures_return_pct =
      100 * mean(weekly_return) * 52,
    annualized_futures_volatility_pct =
      100 * sd(weekly_return) * sqrt(52),
    information_ratio = if (sd(weekly_return) > 0) {
      sqrt(52) * mean(weekly_return) / sd(weekly_return)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    max_futures_drawdown_pct = 100 * min(drawdown),
    active_weeks = sum(simulation$position != 0L),
    completed_trades = sum(trade_log$completed),
    trade_episodes = nrow(trade_log),
    trade_hit_rate_pct = if (nrow(trade_log)) 100 * mean(trade_log$net_pnl > 0) else NA_real_,
    average_holding_weeks = if (nrow(trade_log)) mean(trade_log$holding_weeks) else NA_real_,
    best_trade_pnl = best_trade,
    net_without_best_trade = total_net - best_trade,
    best_year_pnl = best_year,
    net_without_best_year = total_net - best_year,
    max_stress_margin_utilization_pct = 100 * max(simulation$stress_utilization),
    margin_cap_bindings = sum(simulation$margin_cap_binding),
    maintenance_calls = sum(simulation$maintenance_call),
    tbill_pnl = sum(simulation$tbill_pnl),
    ending_capital = tail(simulation$capital_end, 1L),
    account_cagr_pct = 100 * (
      (tail(simulation$capital_end, 1L) / INITIAL_CAPITAL)^(1 / period_years) - 1
    ),
    annualized_account_volatility_pct =
      100 * sd(account_return) * sqrt(52),
    account_sharpe_ratio = if (sd(account_excess_return) > 0) {
      mean(account_excess_return) / sd(account_excess_return) * sqrt(52)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    max_account_drawdown_pct = 100 * min(account_drawdown)
  )
}

# Period summaries preserve the capital actually available at the start of the
# selected interval while resetting only the futures-P&L drawdown reference.
summarize_period <- function(simulation, full_trade_log, start_date, end_date, label) {
  in_period <- simulation$date >= start_date & simulation$date <= end_date
  period_data <- simulation[in_period, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(period_data)) stop("Empty reporting period: ", label)

  period_start_capital <- period_data$capital_start[1L]
  weekly_return <- period_data$net_pnl / period_data$capital_start
  futures_wealth <- period_start_capital + cumsum(period_data$net_pnl)
  drawdown <- futures_wealth /
    cummax(c(period_start_capital, futures_wealth))[-1L] - 1
  account_pnl <- period_data$net_pnl + period_data$tbill_pnl
  account_return <- account_pnl / period_data$capital_start
  account_excess_return <- account_return - period_data$tbill_rate_weekly
  account_peak <- cummax(
    c(period_start_capital, period_data$capital_end)
  )[-1L]
  account_drawdown <- period_data$capital_end / account_peak - 1
  period_years <- nrow(period_data) / 52
  active <- period_data$position != 0L
  annual <- aggregate(net_pnl ~ trading_year, data = period_data, FUN = sum)
  entered_trades <- full_trade_log[
    full_trade_log$entry_date >= start_date & full_trade_log$entry_date <= end_date,
    , drop = FALSE
  ]

  data.frame(
    period = label,
    start_date = min(period_data$date),
    end_date = max(period_data$date),
    weeks = nrow(period_data),
    gross_pnl = sum(period_data$gross_pnl),
    transaction_cost = sum(period_data$transaction_cost),
    net_futures_pnl = sum(period_data$net_pnl),
    total_account_pnl = sum(account_pnl),
    net_futures_return_on_start_pct =
      100 * sum(period_data$net_pnl) / period_start_capital,
    annualized_mean_futures_return_pct =
      100 * mean(weekly_return) * 52,
    annualized_futures_volatility_pct =
      100 * sd(weekly_return) * sqrt(52),
    information_ratio = if (sd(weekly_return) > 0) {
      sqrt(52) * mean(weekly_return) / sd(weekly_return)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    max_futures_drawdown_pct = 100 * min(drawdown),
    active_weeks = sum(active),
    active_week_share = mean(active),
    trades_entered = nrow(entered_trades),
    average_holding_weeks = if (nrow(entered_trades)) {
      mean(entered_trades$holding_weeks)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    max_stress_margin_utilization_pct = 100 * max(period_data$stress_utilization),
    margin_cap_bindings = sum(period_data$margin_cap_binding),
    maintenance_calls = sum(period_data$maintenance_call),
    minimum_contracts_when_active = if (any(active)) {
      min(period_data$contracts[active])
    } else {
      0
    },
    average_contracts_when_active = if (any(active)) {
      mean(period_data$contracts[active])
    } else {
      0
    },
    maximum_contracts = max(period_data$contracts),
    long_weeks = sum(period_data$position > 0L),
    short_weeks = sum(period_data$position < 0L),
    flat_weeks = sum(period_data$position == 0L),
    tbill_pnl = sum(period_data$tbill_pnl),
    start_capital = period_start_capital,
    ending_capital = tail(period_data$capital_end, 1L),
    account_cagr_pct = 100 * (
      (tail(period_data$capital_end, 1L) / period_start_capital)^(1 / period_years) - 1
    ),
    annualized_account_volatility_pct =
      100 * sd(account_return) * sqrt(52),
    account_sharpe_ratio = if (sd(account_excess_return) > 0) {
      mean(account_excess_return) / sd(account_excess_return) * sqrt(52)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    max_account_drawdown_pct = 100 * min(account_drawdown),
    best_year_pnl = max(annual$net_pnl)
  )
}

candidate_id <- function(entry, exit, time_stop) {
  stop_text <- if (is.infinite(time_stop)) "none" else sprintf("%02dw", as.integer(time_stop))
  sprintf("E%03d_X%03d_T%s", round(entry * 100), round(exit * 100), stop_text)
}

# Run one rule on whichever data set is supplied. During selection, this is
# always calibration_ref; full_ref is passed only after the winner is frozen.
run_candidate <- function(data, entry, exit, time_stop,
                          sizing_mode = "unit", ema_half_life = 26L,
                          cost_cl1 = BASE_COST_CL1, cost_cl17 = BASE_COST_CL17) {
  signal <- generate_threshold_positions(data$decision_z, entry, exit, time_stop)
  simulation <- simulate_portfolio(
    data = data,
    position = signal$position,
    sizing_mode = sizing_mode,
    ema_half_life = ema_half_life,
    cost_cl1 = cost_cl1,
    cost_cl17 = cost_cl17
  )
  trade_log <- build_trade_log(simulation)

  list(
    id = candidate_id(entry, exit, time_stop),
    signal = signal,
    weekly = simulation,
    trades = trade_log,
    summary = summarize_simulation(simulation, trade_log)
  )
}

# Verify that the reconstructed decision timing exactly reproduces the raw
# directional holdings created inside the annual SS2000 loop.
raw_full_position <- generate_signal_only(full_ref$decision_z)
if (!identical(raw_full_position, as.integer(full_ref$held_pos_CL1))) {
  stop("Raw-signal decision timing does not reproduce the annual engine")
}

```

### 8.3 Baselines

Baseline A isolates the economic content of the SS2000 signal with exactly one
spread. Baseline B adds only the fixed-at-entry risk-sizing rule. These are useful
for separating signal quality from the effect of taking more or less exposure.

```{r baselines, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

raw_calibration_position <- generate_signal_only(calibration_ref$decision_z)

# Baseline A: no thresholds, no time stop and one spread at all times.
baseline_a_calibration <- simulate_portfolio(
  data = calibration_ref,
  position = raw_calibration_position,
  sizing_mode = "unit"
)
baseline_a_calibration_trades <- build_trade_log(baseline_a_calibration)

# Baseline B: the identical raw direction with fixed-at-entry range sizing.
baseline_b_calibration <- simulate_portfolio(
  data = calibration_ref,
  position = raw_calibration_position,
  sizing_mode = "fixed_entry",
  ema_half_life = 26L
)
baseline_b_calibration_trades <- build_trade_log(baseline_b_calibration)

baseline_calibration_summary <- rbind(
  cbind(
    strategy = "Baseline A: raw signal, one spread",
    summarize_simulation(baseline_a_calibration, baseline_a_calibration_trades)
  ),
  cbind(
    strategy = "Baseline B: raw signal, fixed-entry sizing",
    summarize_simulation(baseline_b_calibration, baseline_b_calibration_trades)
  )
)

baseline_table <- baseline_calibration_summary %>%
  transmute(
    Strategy = strategy,
    `Net futures P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    `Information ratio` = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Maximum drawdown` = percent(max_futures_drawdown_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Trade episodes` = trade_episodes,
    `Active weeks` = active_weeks
  )

knitr::kable(
  baseline_table,
  caption = "Calibration-period baselines, 2000-2016",
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)

```

### 8.4 Calibration-only timing search

Timing is evaluated with one spread first. This keeps the question narrow:
does waiting for a larger SS2000 deviation and exiting after convergence improve
the signal itself? The broad grid contains 27 pre-specified combinations. A
small local grid around the broad leader is used only to check whether the
result sits in a reasonably stable region.

```{r timing-search, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Broad thresholds are intentionally coarse. They cover weak to strong entry
# signals, partial to full convergence, and three holding-period treatments.
entry_grid <- c(0.50, 1.00, 1.50, 2.00)
exit_grid <- c(0.00, 0.50, 1.00)
time_stop_grid <- c(Inf, 26, 52)

broad_grid <- expand.grid(
  entry = entry_grid,
  exit = exit_grid,
  time_stop = time_stop_grid
) %>%
  filter(exit < entry) %>% # An exit must lie inside its corresponding entry boundary.
  arrange(time_stop, entry, exit)

if (nrow(broad_grid) != 27L) stop("The frozen broad grid must contain 27 rules")

broad_runs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(broad_grid)), function(i) {
  run_candidate(
    data = calibration_ref,
    entry = broad_grid$entry[i],
    exit = broad_grid$exit[i],
    time_stop = broad_grid$time_stop[i],
    sizing_mode = "unit"
  )
})

broad_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(broad_runs), function(i) {
  cbind(
    candidate_id = broad_runs[[i]]$id,
    entry = broad_grid$entry[i],
    exit = broad_grid$exit[i],
    time_stop = if (is.infinite(broad_grid$time_stop[i])) "none" else
      as.character(broad_grid$time_stop[i]),
    broad_runs[[i]]$summary
  )
}))

# A minimum of 15 completed calibration trades prevents a very sparse rule
# from leading the shortlist only because of one or two favourable episodes.
broad_summary$eligible <- with(
  broad_summary,
  completed_trades >= 15L & margin_cap_bindings == 0L & maintenance_calls == 0L
)
broad_leader_pool <- broad_summary[broad_summary$eligible, , drop = FALSE]
if (!nrow(broad_leader_pool)) stop("No broad rule meets the minimum evidence requirement")
broad_leader_pool <- broad_leader_pool[order(-broad_leader_pool$net_futures_pnl), ]
broad_centre <- broad_leader_pool[1L, , drop = FALSE]

# The local check uses +/-0.25 around the broad-leading entry and exit. It is
# diagnostic rather than a second opportunity to chase the highest P&L cell.
local_entries <- sort(unique(c(
  broad_centre$entry - 0.25, broad_centre$entry, broad_centre$entry + 0.25
)))
local_exits <- sort(unique(c(
  broad_centre$exit - 0.25, broad_centre$exit, broad_centre$exit + 0.25
)))
local_grid <- expand.grid(
  entry = local_entries,
  exit = local_exits,
  time_stop = time_stop_grid
) %>%
  filter(entry > 0, exit >= 0, exit < entry) %>%
  arrange(time_stop, entry, exit)

local_runs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(local_grid)), function(i) {
  run_candidate(
    data = calibration_ref,
    entry = local_grid$entry[i],
    exit = local_grid$exit[i],
    time_stop = local_grid$time_stop[i],
    sizing_mode = "unit"
  )
})

local_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(local_runs), function(i) {
  cbind(
    candidate_id = local_runs[[i]]$id,
    entry = local_grid$entry[i],
    exit = local_grid$exit[i],
    time_stop = if (is.infinite(local_grid$time_stop[i])) "none" else
      as.character(local_grid$time_stop[i]),
    local_runs[[i]]$summary
  )
}))

# Keep the broad-leading entry/exit pair and compare its three pre-specified
# holding rules after realistic sizing. Local cells describe sensitivity only.
timing_shortlist <- broad_summary %>%
  filter(
    entry == broad_centre$entry,
    exit == broad_centre$exit,
    eligible
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(net_futures_pnl)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)

if (!nrow(timing_shortlist) || nrow(timing_shortlist) > 3L) {
  stop("Timing shortlist is empty or too large")
}

# Heatmaps display all valid broad cells instead of only the winning rule.
broad_plot_data <- broad_summary %>%
  mutate(
    time_stop = factor(time_stop, levels = c("none", "26", "52"),
                       labels = c("No time stop", "26 weeks", "52 weeks")),
    entry_label = factor(entry, levels = entry_grid),
    exit_label = factor(exit, levels = exit_grid),
    net_pnl_thousands = net_futures_pnl / 1000
  )

ggplot(broad_plot_data, aes(entry_label, exit_label, fill = net_pnl_thousands)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = number(net_pnl_thousands, accuracy = 0.1)), size = 3.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ time_stop, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#A33A32", mid = "#F3EBDD", high = "#1F6A5A", midpoint = 0,
    name = "Net P&L\n($000)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Calibration timing grid",
    subtitle = "One-spread results, 2000-2016; blank combinations are invalid by construction",
    x = "Entry threshold |z|", y = "Exit boundary |z|"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

top_broad_table <- broad_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(net_futures_pnl)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  transmute(
    Candidate = candidate_id,
    Entry = entry,
    Exit = exit,
    `Time stop` = time_stop,
    `Net P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    IR = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Max drawdown` = percent(max_futures_drawdown_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
    Trades = completed_trades
  )

knitr::kable(
  top_broad_table,
  caption = "Ten strongest broad-grid rules in the calibration period",
  align = c("l", rep("r", 7))
)

```

### 8.5 Apply sizing and freeze the winner

Only shortlisted timing rules receive the more sophisticated sizing. The
primary implementation fixes contracts at entry and uses a 26-week half-life.
The 13- and 52-week alternatives and weekly resizing are sensitivity checks;
they do not replace the primary rule merely because one happens to earn more.

```{r sizing-and-freeze, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

sizing_design <- data.frame(
  sizing_mode = c("fixed_entry", "fixed_entry", "fixed_entry", "weekly_resize"),
  ema_half_life = c(26L, 13L, 52L, 26L),
  role = c("primary", "half-life sensitivity", "half-life sensitivity", "resizing sensitivity")
)

sizing_runs <- list()
sizing_rows <- list()
run_index <- 0L

for (i in seq_len(nrow(timing_shortlist))) {
  stop_value <- if (timing_shortlist$time_stop[i] == "none") Inf else
    as.numeric(timing_shortlist$time_stop[i])

  for (j in seq_len(nrow(sizing_design))) {
    run_index <- run_index + 1L
    run <- run_candidate(
      data = calibration_ref,
      entry = timing_shortlist$entry[i],
      exit = timing_shortlist$exit[i],
      time_stop = stop_value,
      sizing_mode = sizing_design$sizing_mode[j],
      ema_half_life = sizing_design$ema_half_life[j]
    )

    implementation_id <- paste(
      run$id,
      sizing_design$sizing_mode[j],
      paste0("HL", sizing_design$ema_half_life[j]),
      sep = "__"
    )
    sizing_runs[[implementation_id]] <- run
    sizing_rows[[run_index]] <- cbind(
      implementation_id = implementation_id,
      candidate_id = run$id,
      entry = timing_shortlist$entry[i],
      exit = timing_shortlist$exit[i],
      time_stop = timing_shortlist$time_stop[i],
      sizing_mode = sizing_design$sizing_mode[j],
      ema_half_life = sizing_design$ema_half_life[j],
      research_role = sizing_design$role[j],
      run$summary
    )
  }
}

sizing_summary <- do.call(rbind, sizing_rows)

# The winner is selected only among the three primary fixed-entry, 26-week
# implementations. Profitability is the ranking statistic; trade count, margin
# feasibility and concentration are reported as safeguards rather than blended
# into an opaque composite score.
primary_candidates <- sizing_summary %>%
  filter(
    research_role == "primary",
    net_futures_pnl > 0,
    completed_trades >= 15,
    margin_cap_bindings == 0,
    maintenance_calls == 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(net_futures_pnl))

if (!nrow(primary_candidates)) stop("No primary implementation is eligible")

frozen_selection <- primary_candidates[1L, , drop = FALSE]
frozen_selection$concentration_warning <- with(
  frozen_selection,
  net_without_best_trade <= 0 | net_without_best_year <= 0
)
frozen_selection$selected_using <- "Calibration data through 2016-12-31 only"

# Save the choice before changing the reference to the full 2000-2025 period.
write.csv(
  frozen_selection,
  file.path(PATH_OUTPUT, "frozen_selected_specification.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

primary_table <- primary_candidates %>%
  transmute(
    Candidate = candidate_id,
    Entry = entry,
    Exit = exit,
    `Time stop` = time_stop,
    `Net P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    IR = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Max drawdown` = percent(max_futures_drawdown_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
    Trades = completed_trades,
    `Net without best trade` = dollar(net_without_best_trade, accuracy = 1)
  )

knitr::kable(
  primary_table,
  caption = "Primary sized candidates used for the final calibration choice",
  align = c("l", rep("r", 8))
)

cat(
  "The frozen rule is **", frozen_selection$candidate_id, "**: enter at |z| = ",
  frozen_selection$entry, ", exit at |z| = ", frozen_selection$exit,
  ", and close after ", frozen_selection$time_stop,
  " weeks if convergence has not occurred. This statement is written before any OOS calculation below.",
  sep = ""
)

```

## Step 9: Frozen Strategy Evaluation

Only now is the frozen rule applied to the complete live period. The
2017--2025 result is therefore a single out-of-sample evaluation,
not another round of parameter selection.

```{r final-strategy, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

selected_time_stop <- if (frozen_selection$time_stop == "none") Inf else
  as.numeric(frozen_selection$time_stop)

selected_full_run <- run_candidate(
  data = full_ref,
  entry = frozen_selection$entry,
  exit = frozen_selection$exit,
  time_stop = selected_time_stop,
  sizing_mode = "fixed_entry",
  ema_half_life = 26L
)

selected_weekly <- selected_full_run$weekly
selected_trades <- selected_full_run$trades

# These three rows are the main strategy evidence used in the thesis.
selected_period_summary <- rbind(
  summarize_period(
    selected_weekly, selected_trades,
    min(selected_weekly$date), CALIBRATION_END, "Calibration 2000-2016"
  ),
  summarize_period(
    selected_weekly, selected_trades,
    OOS_START, max(selected_weekly$date), "Out-of-sample 2017-2025"
  ),
  summarize_period(
    selected_weekly, selected_trades,
    min(selected_weekly$date), max(selected_weekly$date), "Full 2000-2025"
  )
)

selected_performance_table <- selected_period_summary %>%
  transmute(
    Period = period,
    `Gross P&L` = dollar(gross_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    Costs = dollar(transaction_cost, accuracy = 1),
    `Net futures P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    IR = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Max drawdown` = percent(max_futures_drawdown_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Active weeks` = active_weeks,
    `Trades entered` = trades_entered,
    `Average holding` = number(average_holding_weeks, accuracy = 0.1)
  )

knitr::kable(
  selected_performance_table,
  caption = "Frozen strategy performance",
  align = c("l", rep("r", 8))
)

```

The table deliberately reports futures P&L separately from collateral
interest. T-bill income is part of ending capital, but it is not evidence that
the trading signal earns an excess return.

### 9.1 Comparison with the two baselines

```{r baseline-comparison, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Recompute both baselines on the full reference with the same cost and margin
# assumptions used for the final strategy.
baseline_a_full <- simulate_portfolio(
  full_ref, raw_full_position, sizing_mode = "unit"
)
baseline_a_full_trades <- build_trade_log(baseline_a_full)

baseline_b_full <- simulate_portfolio(
  full_ref, raw_full_position, sizing_mode = "fixed_entry", ema_half_life = 26L
)
baseline_b_full_trades <- build_trade_log(baseline_b_full)

# Apply the frozen entry, exit and time-stop rule with one spread. This keeps
# the timing effect separate from the final fixed-at-entry position sizing.
selected_unit_full_run <- run_candidate(
  data = full_ref,
  entry = frozen_selection$entry,
  exit = frozen_selection$exit,
  time_stop = selected_time_stop,
  sizing_mode = "unit",
  ema_half_life = 26L
)
selected_unit_full <- selected_unit_full_run$weekly
selected_unit_full_trades <- selected_unit_full_run$trades

make_three_periods <- function(simulation, trades, strategy_name) {
  rbind(
    cbind(strategy = strategy_name, summarize_period(
      simulation, trades, min(simulation$date), CALIBRATION_END, "Calibration 2000-2016"
    )),
    cbind(strategy = strategy_name, summarize_period(
      simulation, trades, OOS_START, max(simulation$date), "Out-of-sample 2017-2025"
    )),
    cbind(strategy = strategy_name, summarize_period(
      simulation, trades, min(simulation$date), max(simulation$date), "Full 2000-2025"
    ))
  )
}

benchmark_period_summary <- rbind(
  make_three_periods(
    baseline_a_full, baseline_a_full_trades, "Baseline A: one spread"
  ),
  make_three_periods(
    baseline_b_full, baseline_b_full_trades, "Baseline B: fixed-entry sizing"
  ),
  cbind(strategy = "Frozen threshold strategy", selected_period_summary)
)

# This long-form dataset contains the four economically distinct stages needed
# for the Chapter 5 overview.
thesis_strategy_period_summary <- rbind(
  make_three_periods(
    baseline_a_full,
    baseline_a_full_trades,
    "Raw signal, one spread"
  ),
  make_three_periods(
    baseline_b_full,
    baseline_b_full_trades,
    "Raw signal, fixed-entry sizing"
  ),
  make_three_periods(
    selected_unit_full,
    selected_unit_full_trades,
    "Optimised timing, one spread"
  ),
  cbind(
    strategy = "Final optimised strategy, fixed-entry sizing",
    selected_period_summary
  )
)

# One numeric overview table supports the compact main-text presentation. It
# reports futures P&L for all three periods and account risk/return measures for
# the out-of-sample and full periods. The long-form dataset above retains every
# underlying component, including T-bill income and trading activity.
rv_main_results_table <- thesis_strategy_period_summary %>%
  mutate(
    period_key = case_when(
      period == "Calibration 2000-2016" ~ "calibration",

    ),
    names_glue = "{period_key}_{.value}"
  ) %>%
  select(

    full_net_futures_pnl,
    oos_total_account_pnl,
    full_total_account_pnl,
    oos_account_cagr_pct,
    oos_annualized_account_volatility_pct,
    oos_account_sharpe_ratio,

    full_account_cagr_pct,
    full_annualized_account_volatility_pct,
    full_account_sharpe_ratio,
    full_max_account_drawdown_pct
  )

rv_main_results_display <- rv_main_results_table %>%
  transmute(
```

### 9.3 Trades, direction and time out of the market

```{r trade-analysis, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.height=5.3}

# Attribution is based on the date a trade is entered. This avoids splitting a
# single economic episode at an arbitrary calendar boundary.
selected_trade_attribution <- selected_trades %>%
  mutate(
    entry_period = case_when(
      entry_date <= CALIBRATION_END ~ "Calibration 2000-2016",
      TRUE ~ "Out-of-sample 2017-2025"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(entry_period, direction) %>%
  summarise(
    trade_episodes = n(),
    net_pnl = sum(net_pnl),
    hit_rate_pct = 100 * mean(net_pnl > 0),
    average_holding_weeks = mean(holding_weeks),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

attribution_table <- selected_trade_attribution %>%
  transmute(
    Period = entry_period,
    Direction = str_to_title(direction),
    Trades = trade_episodes,
    `Net P&L` = dollar(net_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    `Hit rate` = percent(hit_rate_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Average holding` = number(average_holding_weeks, accuracy = 0.1)
  )

knitr::kable(
  attribution_table,
  caption = "Trade-level long/short attribution by entry period",
  align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 4))
)

# Maximum consecutive flat weeks helps distinguish a low trade count caused by
# long holdings from one caused by extended periods without an entry signal.
longest_run <- function(condition) {
  runs <- rle(condition)
  if (!any(runs$values)) return(0L)
  max(runs$lengths[runs$values])
}

activity_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(selected_weekly, selected_weekly$date >= OOS_START),
  function(x) data.frame(
    period = if (min(x$date) >= OOS_START) {
      "Out-of-sample 2017-2025"
    } else {
      "Calibration 2000-2016"
    },
    weeks = nrow(x),
    active_weeks = sum(x$position != 0L),
    active_share_pct = 100 * mean(x$position != 0L),
    longest_flat_run_weeks = longest_run(x$position == 0L)
  )
))

activity_table <- activity_summary %>%
  transmute(
    Period = period,
    Weeks = weeks,
    `Active weeks` = active_weeks,
    `Active share` = percent(active_share_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Longest flat run` = longest_flat_run_weeks
  )

knitr::kable(
  activity_table,
  caption = "Trading activity and time spent out of the market",
  align = c("l", rep("r", 4))
)

# Position-coloured signal points make the entry, exit and inactive regions
# visible without adding a second panel or a smoothed series.

  mutate(position_label = factor(
    position, levels = c(-1, 0, 1), labels = c("Short spread", "Flat", "Long spread")
  ))

ggplot(signal_plot_data, aes(date, decision_z)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-frozen_selection$entry, frozen_selection$entry),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#B4402F", linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-frozen_selection$exit, frozen_selection$exit),
             linetype = "dotted", colour = "#55756D", linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_line(colour = "#8C8C8C", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = position_label), size = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = OOS_START, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#174A5B") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Short spread" = "#B4402F", "Flat" = "#B8B3A9", "Long spread" = "#174A5B"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Decision z-score and weekly position",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines are entry thresholds; dotted lines are exit boundaries",
    x = NULL, y = "Decision z-score", colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
```

## Step 10: Post-Freeze Robustness

The checks in this section are run after the strategy is frozen. They help
interpret implementation risk and economic attribution, but none is allowed to
change the selected entry, exit or time-stop parameters.

### 10.1 Sizing sensitivity

```{r sizing-sensitivity, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

selected_sizing_sensitivity <- sizing_summary %>%
  filter(candidate_id == frozen_selection$candidate_id) %>%
  transmute(
    Implementation = case_when(
      sizing_mode == "fixed_entry" & ema_half_life == 26L ~ "Primary: fixed at entry, HL 26",
      sizing_mode == "fixed_entry" ~ paste0("Fixed at entry, HL ", ema_half_life),
      TRUE ~ paste0("Weekly resize, HL ", ema_half_life)
    ),
    Role = research_role,
    `Net P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    IR = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Max drawdown` = percent(max_futures_drawdown_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
    Costs = dollar(transaction_cost, accuracy = 1),
    Trades = completed_trades
  )

knitr::kable(
  selected_sizing_sensitivity,
  caption = "Calibration sizing sensitivity for the frozen timing rule",
  align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 5))
)

```

The half-life comparison is interpreted as a robustness check around the
chosen six-month compromise. Weekly resizing is not promoted to the main rule
even when its calibration P&L is higher: it changes exposure throughout a
trade and was pre-specified only as an implementation sensitivity. Promoting it
after seeing the calibration result would break the pre-specified selection rule.

### 10.2 Transaction-cost sensitivity

The base case uses the $12.50 / $22.50 per-side cost structure. Low and stress
values are shown only to indicate how much the conclusion depends on execution
quality; they were not used to select the rule.

```{r cost-sensitivity, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

cost_design <- data.frame(
  scenario = c("Low", "Base", "Stress"),
  cost_cl1 = c(7.50, BASE_COST_CL1, 22.50),
  cost_cl17 = c(12.50, BASE_COST_CL17, 42.50)
)

cost_sensitivity_rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(cost_design)), function(i) {
  run <- run_candidate(
    data = full_ref,
    entry = frozen_selection$entry,
    exit = frozen_selection$exit,
    time_stop = selected_time_stop,
    sizing_mode = "fixed_entry",
    ema_half_life = 26L,
    cost_cl1 = cost_design$cost_cl1[i],
    cost_cl17 = cost_design$cost_cl17[i]
  )

  rbind(
    cbind(scenario = cost_design$scenario[i], summarize_period(
      run$weekly, run$trades, min(full_ref$date), CALIBRATION_END,
      "Calibration 2000-2016"
    )),
    cbind(scenario = cost_design$scenario[i], summarize_period(
      run$weekly, run$trades, OOS_START, max(full_ref$date),
      "Out-of-sample 2017-2025"
    ))
  )
})
cost_sensitivity <- do.call(rbind, cost_sensitivity_rows)

cost_sensitivity_table <- cost_sensitivity %>%
  transmute(
    Scenario = scenario,
    Period = period,
    `Net futures P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    Costs = dollar(transaction_cost, accuracy = 1),
    IR = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Max drawdown` = percent(max_futures_drawdown_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1)
  )

knitr::kable(
  cost_sensitivity_table,
  caption = "Post-freeze transaction-cost sensitivity",
  align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 4))
)

```

### 10.3 Unconditional short-spread diagnostic

The strategy's P&L is concentrated in short-spread trades. The following
benchmark asks whether an investor could obtain the same result by staying
short CL1 / long CL17 without using the SS2000 timing signal. The unit version
holds one spread; the risk-managed version resizes weekly because a permanently
open trade otherwise has no new entry at which to refresh its quantity. It is
therefore an attribution diagnostic, not a competing optimized strategy.

```{r unconditional-short, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

always_short_position <- rep(-1L, nrow(full_ref))

unconditional_short_unit <- simulate_portfolio(
  full_ref, always_short_position, sizing_mode = "unit"
) %>%
  add_terminal_liquidation(BASE_COST_CL1, BASE_COST_CL17)
unconditional_short_unit_trades <-
  build_liquidated_trade_log(unconditional_short_unit)

unconditional_short_risk <- simulate_portfolio(
  full_ref, always_short_position, sizing_mode = "weekly_resize", ema_half_life = 26L
) %>%
  add_terminal_liquidation(BASE_COST_CL1, BASE_COST_CL17)
unconditional_short_risk_trades <-
  build_liquidated_trade_log(unconditional_short_risk)

short_benchmark_periods <- rbind(
  make_three_periods(
    unconditional_short_unit,
    unconditional_short_unit_trades,
    "Always short: one spread"
  ),
  make_three_periods(
    unconditional_short_risk,
    unconditional_short_risk_trades,
    "Always short: weekly risk-managed"
  )
)

short_oos_table <- short_benchmark_periods %>%
  filter(period == "Out-of-sample 2017-2025") %>%
  transmute(
    Benchmark = strategy,
    `Net futures P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    Costs = dollar(transaction_cost, accuracy = 1),
    IR = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Max drawdown` = percent(max_futures_drawdown_pct / 100, accuracy = 0.1)
  )

knitr::kable(
  short_oos_table,
  caption = "Out-of-sample unconditional short-spread diagnostic",
  align = c("l", rep("r", 4))
)

```

```{r concentration, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
selected_full_summary <- summarize_simulation(selected_weekly, selected_trades)

concentration_table <- data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Full-sample net futures P&L",
    "Net P&L after removing the best trade",
    "Net P&L after removing the best year",
    "Best trade",
    "Best year"
  ),
  Value = dollar(c(
    selected_full_summary$net_futures_pnl,
    selected_full_summary$net_without_best_trade,

    selected_full_summary$best_year_pnl
  ), accuracy = 1)
)

knitr::kable(
  concentration_table,
  caption = "Concentration diagnostics for the frozen strategy",
  align = c("l", "r")
)

# Show the local neighbourhood around the selected entry/exit rather than only
# reporting the highest cell. Smooth neighbouring outcomes are more credible
# than an isolated optimum.
local_selected_region <- local_summary %>%
  filter(time_stop == frozen_selection$time_stop) %>%
  transmute(
    Entry = entry,
    Exit = exit,
    `Net P&L` = dollar(net_futures_pnl, accuracy = 1),
    IR = number(information_ratio, accuracy = 0.001),
    Trades = completed_trades
  ) %>%
  arrange(Entry, Exit)

knitr::kable(
  local_selected_region,
  caption = "Local calibration neighbourhood for the frozen 52-week holding rule",
  align = c("r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

## Step 11: Complete Appendix Results and Saved Outputs

For completeness, every broad and local timing rule is now evaluated on the
full sample. These calculations occur after the selected OOS result and are
saved for the appendix only. They cannot be used to replace the frozen rule.

```{r appendix-candidates, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# Combine broad and local definitions while removing rules that appear in both.
all_timing_definitions <- unique(rbind(
  data.frame(
    candidate_id = mapply(
      candidate_id, broad_grid$entry, broad_grid$exit, broad_grid$time_stop,
      USE.NAMES = FALSE
    ),
    entry = broad_grid$entry,
    exit = broad_grid$exit,
    time_stop = broad_grid$time_stop,
    candidate_family = "broad"
  ),
  data.frame(
    candidate_id = mapply(
      candidate_id, local_grid$entry, local_grid$exit, local_grid$time_stop,
      USE.NAMES = FALSE
    ),
    entry = local_grid$entry,
    exit = local_grid$exit,
    time_stop = local_grid$time_stop,
    candidate_family = "local"
  )
))
all_timing_definitions <- all_timing_definitions[
  !duplicated(all_timing_definitions$candidate_id), , drop = FALSE
]

appendix_timing_runs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(all_timing_definitions)), function(i) {
  run_candidate(
    data = full_ref,
    entry = all_timing_definitions$entry[i],
    exit = all_timing_definitions$exit[i],
    time_stop = all_timing_definitions$time_stop[i],
    sizing_mode = "unit"
  )
})

appendix_timing_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(appendix_timing_runs), function(i) {
  run <- appendix_timing_runs[[i]]
  cbind(all_timing_definitions[i, ], run$summary)
}))

appendix_timing_periods <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(appendix_timing_runs), function(i) {
  run <- appendix_timing_runs[[i]]
  periods <- rbind(
    summarize_period(
      run$weekly, run$trades, min(full_ref$date), CALIBRATION_END,
      "Calibration 2000-2016"
    ),
    summarize_period(
      run$weekly, run$trades, OOS_START, max(full_ref$date),
      "Out-of-sample 2017-2025"
    ),
    summarize_period(
      run$weekly, run$trades, min(full_ref$date), max(full_ref$date),
      "Full 2000-2025"
    )
  )
  cbind(candidate_id = all_timing_definitions$candidate_id[i], periods)
}))

# Repeat all shortlisted sizing implementations on the full sample only after
# the frozen selected strategy has already been recorded.
appendix_sizing_runs <- list()
appendix_sizing_rows <- list()
appendix_sizing_period_rows <- list()
appendix_index <- 0L

for (i in seq_len(nrow(timing_shortlist))) {
  stop_value <- if (timing_shortlist$time_stop[i] == "none") Inf else
    as.numeric(timing_shortlist$time_stop[i])

  for (j in seq_len(nrow(sizing_design))) {
    appendix_index <- appendix_index + 1L
    run <- run_candidate(
      data = full_ref,
      entry = timing_shortlist$entry[i],
      exit = timing_shortlist$exit[i],
      time_stop = stop_value,
      sizing_mode = sizing_design$sizing_mode[j],
      ema_half_life = sizing_design$ema_half_life[j]
    )
    implementation_id <- paste(
      run$id, sizing_design$sizing_mode[j],
      paste0("HL", sizing_design$ema_half_life[j]), sep = "__"
    )

    appendix_sizing_runs[[implementation_id]] <- run
    appendix_sizing_rows[[appendix_index]] <- cbind(
      implementation_id = implementation_id,
      candidate_id = run$id,
      sizing_mode = sizing_design$sizing_mode[j],
      ema_half_life = sizing_design$ema_half_life[j],
      research_role = sizing_design$role[j],
      run$summary
    )
    appendix_sizing_period_rows[[appendix_index]] <- cbind(
      implementation_id = implementation_id,
      rbind(
        summarize_period(
          run$weekly, run$trades, min(full_ref$date), CALIBRATION_END,
          "Calibration 2000-2016"
        ),
        summarize_period(
          run$weekly, run$trades, OOS_START, max(full_ref$date),
          "Out-of-sample 2017-2025"
        ),
        summarize_period(
          run$weekly, run$trades, min(full_ref$date), max(full_ref$date),
          "Full 2000-2025"
        )
      )
    )
  }
}

appendix_sizing_summary <- do.call(rbind, appendix_sizing_rows)
appendix_sizing_periods <- do.call(rbind, appendix_sizing_period_rows)

```

### 11.1 Implementation checks

```{r implementation-checks, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# These are short reconciliation guards, not a separate model-selection layer.
selected_calibration_row <- selected_period_summary[
  selected_period_summary$period == "Calibration 2000-2016", , drop = FALSE
]

stopifnot(
  nrow(broad_grid) == 27L,
  max(calibration_ref$date) <= CALIBRATION_END,
  min(selected_weekly$date[selected_weekly$date >= OOS_START]) >= OOS_START,
  identical(raw_full_position, as.integer(full_ref$held_pos_CL1)),
  ema_26_error <= 1e-10,
  all(selected_weekly$contracts == floor(selected_weekly$contracts)),
  !any(selected_weekly$maintenance_call),
  abs(selected_calibration_row$net_futures_pnl - frozen_selection$net_futures_pnl) < 1e-8,
  abs(sum(selected_trades$net_pnl) - sum(selected_weekly$net_pnl)) < 1e-8
)

check_table <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Annual raw-signal positions reconstruct exactly",
    "26-week dispersion path reconstructs exactly",
    "Calibration ends before OOS",
    "All selected-strategy contract quantities are integers",
    "Trade log reconciles to weekly net P&L",
    "No maintenance-margin call occurs"
  ),
  Result = rep("Passed", 6)
)

knitr::kable(
  check_table,
  caption = "Core implementation checks",
  align = c("l", "c")
)

```
